English.Char_Desc_80: Open-source download manager that splits files across connections and mirrors
English.Char_Desc_250: Hydra is an open-source download manager and accelerator. It splits each file across many connections and mirrors, moves work from slow connections to fast ones, and resumes interrupted downloads. Includes a desktop app, a CLI and browser add-ons.
English.Char_Desc_450: Hydra is an open-source download manager and accelerator for Windows, macOS and Linux. It splits each file across many connections and independent mirrors, hands unfinished ranges from slow connections to fast ones, and detects stalled connections within seconds. The desktop app has a queue, a scheduler and browser integration for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; the command-line tool understands wget and curl options.
English.Char_Desc_2000:
Hydra Download Manager (HDM) is a free, open-source download manager and accelerator for Windows, macOS and Linux.
Hydra splits every file into ranges and fetches them over many connections at once, from one server or from several independent mirrors of the same file. It keeps rebalancing while the transfer runs: when one connection falls behind, a faster one takes over the rest of its range, so a single slow peer never holds up the finish. Degraded connections are spotted statistically within seconds, long before a socket timeout would fire.
Supported protocols are HTTP, HTTPS and FTP, through HTTP CONNECT and SOCKS4, SOCKS4a or SOCKS5 proxies. Data is written straight to its place in the file, so memory use stays flat whether the download is 10 MB or 10 TB. Downloads can be verified against server-advertised checksums, and optional Reed-Solomon parity protects finished files against bit rot.
The desktop app manages a download queue with categories, a start and stop scheduler, retry tracking, a tray icon and launch at startup. Its interface is translated into 30 languages. Browser extensions for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari hand downloads over to Hydra, including the cookies a site needs for authenticated links.
The hydra command-line tool accepts wget and curl style options, reads Metalink files, and includes an interactive terminal queue manager. The engine is also available as libhydra, a C library for embedding in other applications.
Hydra has no ads, no telemetry and no accounts. The applications are licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later and the engine libraries under MIT or Apache-2.0.
